output.brief: The stops are driven by an interaction between the new firmware (6.4) and the glossy stretch film introduced in August. The firmware now keeps weak short-range reflections, and the glossy film produces them at oblique angles, so the robots treat staged pallets as obstacles. Evidence: in the bench test, 6.4 on gloss film stopped 17/20 passes. 6.3 on gloss, or 6.4 on the old matte film, stopped 0–1/20. In the field, 6.4 pallet robots in Zones A/B went from 3.2 to 15.6 stops per 100 hours. The 6.3 robots working the same zones stayed flat, as did 6.4 tote robots in Zone C, which has no wrapped pallets. Temps were present everywhere, so they do not explain the pattern. A discipline policy would punish the wrong people and hide information. Shortening the protective fields would weaken a safety control without fixing the cause. I'm fairly confident (about 85%). Next steps: switch back to the previous matte film, keep the firmware, and track weekly stops by zone and firmware group. Have Halvane test 6.4.2 against the gloss film before relying on it. Keep the firmware rollback as a fallback if the film switch doesn't bring stops down. The link between stops and missed cut-offs is not proven. Peak volume also contributed, since cut-off misses rose last year with flat stops.
